title: Refactor adapter defaults into method-specific PEFT YAML groups
description: Split the shared adapter/PEFT shell settings from method-specific adapter settings in Hydra config. Keep the user-facing shape as adapter.peft.<method>: {...}, keep branch presence as the normal method selection rule, and move method defaults into method-local YAML files such as configs/_defaults/adapter/peft/lora.yaml and configs/_defaults/adapter/peft/loha.yaml. The default adapter config should still compose a concrete active method instead of leaving adapter mode without method settings.

title: Move method-specific adapter validation out of generic PEFT validation
description: Remove adapter-specific LoHa checks from library/config/config_validation.py. Validation for active adapter branches should flow through method-owned config binding/runtime translation rather than hardcoded adapter names in shared validation. As part of this cleanup, stop relying on LoHa module constructor defaults when adapter.peft.loha.rank is unset; require method-owned config translation to define or reject rank explicitly.

title: Reconcile LoHa bypass-mode with weight decomposition
description: Fix the semantic mismatch between bypass_mode and weight_decompose for the repo-owned LoHa path. Vendored LyCORIS disables bypass mode when DoRA-style weight decomposition is enabled, but the absorbed implementation currently lets bypass_mode win and silently skip the decomposition path. Decide the intended repo-owned behavior, validate incompatible config combinations, and add focused coverage.

title: Validate required LoHa rank in config and runtime
description: Fix the active LoHa rank gap: adapter.peft.loha.rank currently defaults to None while the absorbed LoHa module requires a positive integer rank. Add validation and/or sane defaults so empty or malformed LoHa config fails clearly before runtime construction, and ensure the forward config surface documents whether rank is required or defaulted.

title: Promote PEFT under adapter config and mode
description: Refactor adapter training so PEFT is represented as one adapter family under the adapter concept instead of the root training mode/config surface. Target shape is mode: adapter with adapter.peft.<method> branch selection, avoiding redundant adapter.type and peft.method discriminators when the active branch already names the family/method. Validate exactly one active adapter family and exactly one active PEFT method, then update runtime wiring, Hydra defaults, tests, docs, and compatibility handling as needed.

title: Design a stronger config validation workflow
description: The roadmap calls out config validation as an active TODO. Create a focused follow-up to define how invalid configs should be caught, where validation should live, and what should be covered by tests versus runtime checks. This should produce a concrete plan for validation ownership and the highest-risk missing validations in the active training/config surface.

title: Extract shared model component naming out of parameter_dump.py
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

The repo currently resolves shared public component labels such as denoiser->unet and text_encoder1->clip_l through library/models/parameter_dump.py. That works as a source of truth, but the file name and ownership are now misleading: the naming seam is being reused by startup summaries and resource reporting, not just parameter/state dump formatting.

This should be addressed soon so shared component naming has a clear home before more observability/reporting features depend on the current location.

Scope:
- move the shared model-family component naming contract out of library/models/parameter_dump.py into a more neutral model-owned home
- update current consumers to use the new seam
- keep parameter/state dump formatting layered on top of that shared naming source instead of owning it
- preserve current public labels and behavior for existing dumps, summaries, and startup/resource output

Acceptance criteria:
- shared component naming no longer lives in parameter_dump.py
- current users of resolve_component_names/build_named_components continue to work through the new home
- parameter dump code depends on the extracted naming seam rather than owning it
design: Prefer a narrowly named model-owned module such as component_names.py or similar over another catch-all helper file. Keep the extracted seam focused on public component labels and top-level loaded-component naming, not dump formatting.

title: Design deeper runtime resource attribution for training runs
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done

The current resource monitor gives good phase-level usage tracking and startup parameter accounting, but it does not deeply explain where RAM/VRAM are going during a run. We can see that resources are in use and roughly when they increase, but we cannot yet attribute those increases clearly enough to loaded model weights vs training state vs activations/workspaces vs cache/materialization behavior. This makes it harder to optimize memory behavior confidently, especially when comparing adapter vs fine-tune runs or trying to understand gaps between startup accounting and live usage.

This issue tracks designing a stronger runtime resource-attribution layer that can explain what is actually using memory during a run, even if some of the heavier instrumentation must stay optional for performance reasons.

Scope:
- define the difference between startup structural accounting, actual runtime snapshots, and estimated training-state buckets
- design better startup accounting for adapter mode so loaded base-model residency is visible alongside trainable slices
- design optional deeper attribution for VRAM and RAM during runs, beyond current phase-level totals
- identify useful attribution checkpoints such as post-model-load, post-optimizer-create, first backward, first optimizer step, cache phases, and major train-loop boundaries
- evaluate what can be measured cheaply all the time vs what should live behind an opt-in heavier debug mode
- clarify what kinds of ownership attribution are realistic (component/subsystem/phase) vs not practical to promise

Acceptance criteria:
- there is a documented design direction for deeper runtime resource attribution
- the design explicitly covers both VRAM and RAM
- the design distinguishes always-on low-cost tracking from optional high-cost/debug tracking
- the design addresses adapter-mode visibility of loaded base-model residency
- follow-up implementation work can be split cleanly from the design
design: Prefer extending the existing resource monitor/observability surface instead of inventing a separate parallel subsystem. Keep startup user-facing output understandable during normal bootup, and treat deeper attribution as an optional investigative mode when needed.

title: Harden adapter diagnostics public-label contract
description: Adapter diagnostics currently rely on adapter trainable refs carrying public component labels via ref.component. Add focused tests and/or explicit mapping so adapter startup summaries and reports cannot drift from the fine-tune public label contract across model families.

description: Revisit and refine the strategy contract after implementing the next one or two non-SD diffusion model families. Use the concrete lessons from Flux2 and Anima to separate core required family responsibilities from optional capabilities, tighten payload typing, and identify which current responsibilities belong in strategy versus trainer, data, or objective layers. Keep this issue blocked until those implementation probes land so the refinement is driven by real integration pressure rather than abstract cleanup.

Use the diffusion-pipe Wan implementation as the reference for model loading, multimodal or video-aware preprocessing, latent preparation, text and image conditioning, denoiser inputs, caching, sampling, validation, and checkpoint behavior. This issue should also capture any strategy, data, or orchestration assumptions that are too image-centric for Wan-style diffusion families.

title: Implement Anima model-family integration into the active strategy/trainer path

Use the reference Anima strategy and utilities to map its Qwen3 plus T5 token flow, Qwen text encoding, 16-channel latent path, cache payloads, adapter expectations, sampling, validation, and checkpoint behavior onto the current strategies/trainer architecture. Treat this as both delivery work and a concrete probe of how well the current strategy contract handles a family that is still diffusion-based but structurally less SD-like.

title: Implement Flux2 model-family integration into the active strategy/trainer path
description: Integrate Flux2 as a first-class model family in the active sd-scripts training path. Use the diffusion-pipe reference implementation to map Flux2 loading, latent preparation, conditioning payloads, denoiser call shape, loss target construction, caching implications, sampling, validation, and checkpoint behavior onto the current strategies/trainer architecture. The goal is not just feature parity, but to expose which parts of the current strategy contract are genuinely general for diffusion families and which parts are accidental SD/SDXL/SD3 assumptions.

Follow-up adapter reporting refinement: moved adapter-module counting out of logging inference and into adapter-owned provenance/reporting. Added adapter_module_path to AdapterTrainableParameterRef, shared builder helpers in library/adapters/shared/trainables.py, new library/adapters/shared/reporting.py, and updated repo-owned PEFT runtimes to populate adapter-module identity for reporting consumers. Include how adapter methods contribute metadata, how future artifact manifests consume it, and how existing safetensors metadata keys migrate or remain compatible.

The design should cover what facts are published first, who publishes them, how scope/lifetime and nesting work, how consumers read absent facts safely, and how adapters such as TLora use the API without owning it.

Active diffusion families now publish StrategyContext during denoiser forward, TLora derives timestep masks from strategy context through the PEFT runtime boundary, and focused strategy/runtime tests are green. title: Fix LoRA runtime registry regression tests
Remove remaining adapter-level legacy PEFT config shims
Remove remaining LoRA-specific legacy compatibility surface
Remove obsolete legacy LoRA implementation files after repo-owned refresh
Refresh repo-owned LoRA method against current HF PEFT
description: Investigate the current legacy LoRA path in sd-scripts against the current Hugging Face PEFT LoRA implementation, identify the best repo-owned target shape, and implement or stage the modernization work needed to replace the outdated legacy-2023 behavior with a cleaner current LoRA method.
notes: Initial investigation: current sd-scripts LoRA is still a thin repo-owned shell (library/adapters/methods/peft/lora/config.py + runtime.py) over the older built-in implementation in impl.py, which still owns module discovery, target naming, optimizer grouping, and state dict behavior internally. In contrast, current HF PEFT LoRA on main (cloned 2026-05-03 at commit dc2e5b2d9fdbcea900ae8c2bad120eab035ed41b) is built around per-target layer wrappers and explicit config for rank/alpha patterns, RS-LoRA scaling, DoRA, modern initialization options, bias handling, and richer target selection. Recommended repo-owned direction: do not import PEFT wholesale. Instead absorb the core linear/conv LoRA layer/runtime into our standard method package shape (method-local module/runtime/state-dict, optimization-owned resolved targets), then selectively adopt high-value PEFT semantics: use_rslora, use_dora, rank_pattern/alpha_pattern on selector paths, optional fan_in_fan_out where genuinely needed, and clearer bias/init validation. Lower priority or likely out of scope for first pass: multi-adapter management, target_parameters for arbitrary nn.Parameter, embedding support, quant backend dispatch, Arrow/BD-LoRA/aLoRA/QALoRA, transformer-specific auto target_modules, and other Transformers-centric PEFT integrations.

title: Design LyCORIS norm as an auxiliary PEFT target toggle
description: Follow up on the norm investigation by designing the narrowest repo-owned implementation seam for vendor-style train_norm behavior. The goal is to support LayerNorm/GroupNorm delta modules as an auxiliary target-class toggle layered onto compatible repo-owned LyCORIS-derived PEFT runtimes, without introducing adapter-root sprawl or misrepresenting norm as a standalone mutually exclusive method. Account for current constraints: single adapter_type runtime spec, resolved targets already include norm layers, and adapter.peft.lora is still legacy/unabsorbed.

title: Investigate LyCORIS norm integration shape
description: Investigate how LyCORIS norm support works, whether it should be a standalone PEFT method or an auxiliary target-selection toggle in sd-scripts, and document the recommended fit plus any follow-up seam/design work.
notes: Investigation summary: LyCORIS norm is not really a standalone method in vendor behavior. It is enabled via train_norm=True and swaps in NormModule only for LayerNorm/GroupNorm targets while the chosen main algo still handles Linear/Conv targets. In sd-scripts, resolved adapter targets already include LayerNorm/GroupNorm via library/adapters/runtime/targets.py, but PEFT config/runtime resolution intentionally assumes exactly one active method branch and one adapter_type in AdapterRuntimeSpec. Recommended fit: do not add adapter.peft.norm as a standalone mutually exclusive method branch. Treat norm support as an auxiliary target-class toggle layered onto compatible repo-owned LyCORIS-derived methods, ideally after or alongside a small PEFT helper/composite seam. Near-term caution: current adapter.peft.lora is still a legacy wrapper, so a repo-wide train_norm flag would over-promise support before LoRA is absorbed or a composite runtime seam exists. Vendor references: library/vendor/lycoris/lycoris/modules/norms.py, wrapper.py, kohya.py, docs/Network-Args.md, docs/API.md, Change.md.

Repo-owned BOFT now does this, but repo-owned OFT still appears to leave original bias untouched in the non-bypass merged-weight path. Audit OFT, add biasful target coverage, and either fix merged bias handling or document/guard unsupported cases explicitly.

title: Decide long-term LoHa weight_decompose and bypass_mode semantics

Include config-surface guidance and test coverage for the chosen rule.

title: Define and implement plain dropout semantics for LoHa
description: Clarify what the forward LoHa dropout knob should mean in this repo. Vendored LyCORIS only partially wires plain dropout through bypass-mode behavior and warns that normal LoHa dropout is not really implemented, while the absorbed implementation currently exposes the field without applying it. Decide whether to support vendor-style bypass dropout, define a cleaner repo-owned behavior, or deprecate/remove the field in favor of rank_dropout and module_dropout.

title: Define and implement plain dropout semantics for LoHa
description: Clarify what the forward LoHa  knob should mean in this repo. Decide whether to support vendor-style bypass dropout, define a cleaner repo-owned behavior, or deprecate/remove the field in favor of rank_dropout and module_dropout.

title: Design versioned multi-method adapter artifact format
description: Design a repo-owned saved-adapter artifact format that can eventually hold multiple adapter methods in one file. Define the manifest/versioning story, how method type and method-local settings are represented, how target identity is recorded, and how tensor namespaces should be structured so future LoHa/LoRA/etc. payloads can coexist without relying purely on flat tensor-name conventions.

title: Investigate and document "full bf16" semantics
description: The roadmap explicitly calls out uncertainty around what "full bf16" means in this repo. Audit the active code/config paths that mention or imply full-bf16 behavior, identify the current effective behavior, and document the intended meaning and any mismatches. Add an optional adapter protocol method such as get_diagnostics_components() so adapter types can report their per-component module and parameter allocation, then thread that data into PeftMode training diagnostics without reopening old compatibility-era runtime boundaries.

Use the existing docs_design strategy follow-up notes as supporting context.

Start from current repo-owned target/runtime boundaries, identify which features are method behavior versus backend integration, and create narrower follow-up issues for any candidate worth implementing.

Candidate areas include module naming, supported-target filtering, trainable-ref attachment, save/load loops, missing-key reporting, shared projection/state handling, and loaded-runtime merge wiring. Keep method-specific math and config validation inside method packages.

Add a repo-owned way to express that per-target axis choice through the current target-selection/config surface, with tests and docs, instead of forcing a single global IA3 axis policy.

Include config-surface guidance and focused coverage for the chosen rule.

title: Add first-class DyLoRA rank-resize export support

Implement that as a first-class repo-owned DyLoRA capability in the main code path rather than as a separate side helper: for example, a runtime/module/export option that can intentionally emit a lower-rank LoRA-style payload from a DyLoRA-trained adapter. Keep the behavior inside the active adapter/method ownership boundaries, define how the target rank is requested, and add focused coverage for prefix/block truncation behavior and exported artifact semantics.

title: Investigate BOFT FastBlockDiag optimization path

This is not an algorithm change; it is a possible optimization follow-up if BOFT becomes a measurable hotspot. Evaluate portability, build complexity, fallback behavior, and whether a repo-owned implementation is justified.

title: Evaluate compact OFT upper-triangle parameterization
description: Review whether the repo-owned OFT implementation should switch from storing full square block parameters to storing only the independent upper-triangular values, similar to Hugging Face PEFT's OFT rotation module, while preserving our LyCORIS-aligned Diag-OFT behavior and checkpoint compatibility expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Compare current repo-owned OFT parameter count and checkpoint layout against an upper-triangle-only design.; Decide whether the memory/compute savings justify the extra reconstruction complexity for this repo.; If adopted, preserve or explicitly migrate repo-owned OFT checkpoint compatibility and document the decision in library/adapters/methods/peft/README.md and CHANGELOG.md as appropriate.
notes: Repo guidance: there is currently no meaningful backward-compatibility pressure for repo-owned OFT checkpoints or parameter layouts. Prefer the best native design for this repo first; if old/full-block import support is ever needed later, keep it as explicit compatibility helpers outside the core training pipeline rather than shaping the training/runtime design now. This should be treated as an immediate follow-up after the current OFT landing work, not as distant backlog.

description: Add short repo-owned guidance notes under library/adapters and library/adapters/methods/peft so future work keeps family/method-specific logic out of the adapter upper layer.

title: Explore multi-method PEFT capability within adapter families
description: Explore support for training runs that combine multiple PEFT adapter methods within the same adapter family, especially LyCORIS-shaped combinations. Keep the normal single-method adapter.peft.<method> config path simple, but investigate whether repo-owned helpers or composition seams should support multi-method PEFT runs in the future. This should stay scoped to adapter-family combinations rather than generic cross-family adapter mixing unless a stronger use case appears.

title: Explore method resolution and optimizer grouping for mixed-method adapters
description: Follow up on how adapter method resolution, target ownership, and optimizer grouping should work if a future adapter-family helper can combine multiple PEFT methods in one run. Clarify which method owns each target, how trainable refs and grouping plans should be attributed, and what defaults or helper-owned rules should apply to optimization groups when methods differ.

title: Add shared adapter runtime state controls
description: Explore shared adapter runtime controls that will matter once the repo supports richer saved-adapter artifacts and multiple logical payloads. Consider lightweight enable/disable behavior, explicit reversible merge/unmerge operations, and any minimal active-state concepts needed for future multi-method or multi-payload adapter runtimes without importing PEFT's full wrapper model.

title: Improve adapter load diagnostics and target mismatch reporting
description: Improve repo-owned adapter load/reporting so failures are easier to reason about when target resolution and saved tensors diverge. Cover cases like unsupported targets skipped during load, target names present in a checkpoint but absent from the current model, shape mismatches, and partial method payloads. Prefer shared adapter-loader diagnostics where possible so the behavior benefits more than just LoHa.

title: Expand behavioral test coverage for repo-owned LoHa
description: Broaden focused LoHa test coverage beyond the current linear/tucker round-trip cases. Add behavior tests for Conv1d and Conv3d targets, rs_lora scaling, weight_decompose, wd_on_output=False, bypass_mode, rank_dropout scaling, module dropout, and any finalized plain-dropout behavior. Keep the coverage centered on repo-owned semantics rather than PEFT/LyCORIS parity for its own sake.

title: Document OpenSpec and beads workflow in AGENTS
description: Add AGENTS.md guidance describing when to use OpenSpec versus beads, and clarify that OpenSpec artifacts complement rather than replace bd issue tracking.

title: Document regularization-image usage constraints
description: The roadmap notes that the current reg_data_dir / is_reg flow is mechanically correct but easy to misuse. Add a docs-focused follow-up to explain that regularization images only help when they are genuine class/prior images with matching generic captions or class_tokens, and make sure future examples communicate that clearly.

title: Add adapter diagnostics for method-specific runtime stats
description: Backlog adapter-systems follow-up: decide whether the repo should surface more adapter diagnostics in training/reporting, such as per-component module counts, parameter totals, or method-specific norm summaries. This should be treated as shared adapter infrastructure rather than a LoHa-only requirement, and it should stay secondary to correctness and artifact-format work.
close_reason: Duplicate of sd-scripts-yb1; keeping the more concrete PEFT diagnostics implementation issue.

title: Make LoHa initialization policy explicit
description: Consider making LoHa initialization an explicit repo-owned policy rather than an implicit carry-over from the absorbed LyCORIS behavior. The immediate goal is not PEFT parity, but clearer ownership: document the current initialization choice, decide whether the repo wants named init modes or one fixed policy, and add tests that pin the intended behavior if this is judged worth keeping configurable.

title: Evaluate extracting a dedicated LoHa functional kernel layer
description: Backlog investigation: decide whether the repo-owned LoHa math should stay embedded in the module wrapper or move into a more isolated functional layer. This is low priority and should only move forward if profiling, autograd debugging, or method sharing across runtimes makes the extra indirection worthwhile.
